sentences.text: Monarch butterflies are famous for a journey that is astonishing for such light wings.
In eastern North America, many monarchs fly south in the fall toward mountain forests in central Mexico.
The trip can cover thousands of miles.
The butterflies that reach Mexico are a special long-lived generation.
They spend the winter clustered in the trees, then start north when the season turns.
Most of them do not fly all the way back to the farthest summer places.
They lay eggs on milkweed, and the next generation, then the generation after that, continues the trip.
It can take several generations to fill the summer range again.
Milkweed matters because it is the plant monarch caterpillars eat.
If there is no milkweed, there are no caterpillars, even if adult butterflies can sip nectar from other flowers.
Not every butterfly migrates this way. The monarch's long trip is unusual.
Storms, sudden cold, and the loss of forests and milkweed can all make their numbers smaller.
People help by protecting the winter groves and by leaving milkweed in gardens and along roadsides.
A monarch in a summer field may be the grandchild of one that left Mexico in the spring.
The orange wings look delicate, but the journey is a chain of lives, not a single afternoon.

questions.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?

choices.text: How to paint orange wings on any insect
The long monarch migration and the generations that continue it
Why all butterflies spend winter in one tree
How nectar replaces the need for any plant

questions.explanation: The passage describes the flight to Mexico, the winter rest, and the generations that carry the trip north. That chain is the main idea.

questions.prompt: Where do many eastern monarchs spend the winter?

choices.text: Inside every summer garden
On milkweed the whole year
In mountain forests in central Mexico
At the North Pole

questions.explanation: The passage says many monarchs from eastern North America fly to mountain forests in central Mexico for the winter.

questions.prompt: The butterflies spend winter clustered in the trees. Clustered means what?

choices.text: Flying thousands of miles in one hour
Eating only nectar from roses
Sleeping under the soil
Gathered closely together

questions.explanation: Clustered means gathered closely together. The passage pictures the winter butterflies grouped in the trees.

questions.prompt: A town mows down all its milkweed but plants flowers that adult butterflies like. What can a reader figure out?

choices.text: Caterpillars still will not have their food, so the problem is only partly solved
Caterpillars can eat any bright flower
The winter forests are no longer needed
Migration will become a one-day trip

questions.explanation: Adults may sip nectar from many flowers, but the passage says caterpillars eat milkweed. Flowers alone do not replace that plant.

questions.prompt: Which order matches the big trip?

choices.text: Spend winter in Mexico, fly south, then stop migrating
Fly south, spend winter in Mexico, start north, and later generations continue
Lay all the eggs in Mexico, then fly south for summer
One butterfly flies the whole round trip in a single day

questions.explanation: The passage moves from the fall flight south, to winter in Mexico, to the start north, and then to later generations. That is the order to keep.
